notesStmt.note: This manuscript was likely composed sometime in 1884.
This manuscript contains lines that contributed to "Of That Blithe Throat of Thine," a poem first published in Harper's Monthly Magazine in January 1885 and then included in November Boughs (1888).

The verso contains lines that may be loosely related to the poem "Last of Ebb, and Daylight Waning," which was first published in The Nineteenth Century magazine in August 1885 and then included in November Boughs (1888).

lg.l:
the song of a snow⹀bird merrily sounding
out of amid the desolation.]

Of that blithe throat of thine, cheering sounding
through bleak and blank,
I take mind the lesson, arctic bird—I too will also welcome ice and chill,

Nay, the profoundest chill, as now—a torpid
heart

l.add: Old aag age land-lock'd within its winter bay—(cold cold O cold)

lg.l: These snowy hairs, lameness, a feeble arm
For them thy rule I'll take
